title: Adaptive-scale + error-feedback KV quantization probe for continuous batching
creator: Asha Patel
description: Experiment to evaluate a combined adaptive-scale quantization + error-feedback (residual compensation) strategy for KV cache compression across FP8/INT8/INT4 operating points, measured under continuous batching workloads and typical Redwood production routing policies.
objective: Reduce GPU memory footprint of per-request KV caches while keeping downstream generation quality within an acceptable regression envelope, and measure trade-offs with throughput/latency under continuous batching.
experiment_plan: 1) Implement per-layer adaptive scale estimator for KV activations; 2) Add error-feedback residual buffer to correct low-bit quantization drift across timesteps; 3) Evaluate three quant targets: FP8 (e4m3-like), INT8 (symmetric), INT4 (symmetric with grouped scaling); 4) Integrate into continuous batching microbench harness that simulates mixed sequence-length arrivals and prefix caching; 5) Run sweep across scale-adaptation hyperparams, residual decay, and commit frequency; 6) Collect QoS and quality metrics, analyze cohort-level failure modes; 7) Propose runtime fallback rules for quality-safe rollouts.
workloads: burst traffic with batching enabled (QPS mix)
results_summary: Early probe results (sweep 1): FP8 with adaptive scale + error-feedback incurred negligible quality regression (logit-RMSE < 0.8%, downstream accuracy delta < 0.5%) and provided ~22% KV memory reduction vs FP16 baseline. INT8 gave ~35% memory reduction with modest quality loss (logit-RMSE 1.2–1.8%) that was largely correctable with a small residual buffer (8 bytes per KV slot) and conservative grouped scaling. INT4 achieved highest memory wins (up to 58% reduction) but showed instability on long-context workloads (>2048 tokens) with regression spikes on specific cohorts (instruction-following prompts) even when using aggressive error-feedback; additional mitigation required (layer-prioritized mixed precision). Latency impact was small for FP8/INT8 (<3% p50) but INT4 introduced up to 12% p95 latency variance due to extra dequantization passes and residual accumulation code-paths.
analysis_notes: - Continuous batching effects: compression helps reduce per-batch memory pressure, allowing larger batch sizes, which recovered throughput lost to dequant overhead in INT8 cases. - Error-feedback residuals reduce drift over long prefix chains but add a small persistent state per KV slot; tradeoff favors INT8 for production given current hardware performance. - Certain transformer heads are more sensitive (early cross-attn layers); plan to preserve FP16 for those layers in a hybrid map.
decisions: Promote FP8+adaptive-scale+residual as primary candidate for low-risk rollout (runtime-1.21) for non-sensitive customers.
Implement HEADS_MAP to pin first 2 cross-attn layers to FP16 when using INT4 to avoid catastrophic regressions.
Add a cohort-aware guardrail that triggers automatic fallback to FP16 when per-request logit divergence exceeds threshold for >= 3 requests.
Do not enable INT4 by default for latency-sensitive dedicated pools; mark INT4 as experimental behind feature flag.
next_steps: Run focused long-context sweep with layer-prioritized mixed-precision (FP16 for sensitive layers, INT8/FP8 elsewhere) and 10k-chat holdout.
Benchmark on dedicated A100/RTX8000 fleet to measure real dequant kernel overheads and optimize CUDA kernels for grouped INT4 dequant.
Add automated regression alerts to console tied to regression-set prompts and integrate with rollout policy to auto-roll back.
Prepare RFC for ops-runbooks describing fallback triggers and reserved memory accounting changes.
blockers: Need specialized A/B fleet with deterministic continuous batching to reproduce long-context instability (infra ticket: ENG-91411)
CUDA kernel engineer bandwidth for grouped INT4 optimized kernels is limited this sprint
